sections.body: The days of the week repeat in a cycle of 7. If today is Monday, then 7 days later it is Monday again. So is 14 days later, 21 days later and 28 days later.
This gives a shortcut. To find the day after many days, find how many days are left over after taking away whole weeks. Divide by 7 and look at the remainder.
Example: today is Friday. What day is it in 9 days? 9 ÷ 7 = 1 remainder 2. One whole week brings us back to Friday, then 2 more days: Saturday, Sunday. It is Sunday.
Another: today is Wednesday and we want 15 days on. 15 ÷ 7 = 2 remainder 1. Two weeks bring us back to Wednesday. One more day is Thursday.
Pick any day of the week and a number of days, such as 25. Find the remainder after dividing by 7, then count on that many days from your day. Check with a real calendar.
This is the idea behind 'clock arithmetic' (modular arithmetic) and prepares for the Doomsday method later. Start with small numbers and a real calendar, then try bigger jumps.

quiz.q: Today is Tuesday. What day will it be in 21 days?
hints: 21 days is a number of whole weeks. How many?
Example: from Sunday, 14 days on is 2 whole weeks, so it is the same day again. Do the same with 21 days.
quiz.explain: 21 is 3 whole weeks with no days left over, so it is the same day of the week.

quiz.q: Today is Monday. What day will it be in 10 days?
hints: Take away one whole week first (7 days).
10 ÷ 7 = 1 remainder 3. Count on 3 days from today.
Example: from Friday, 9 days on is 1 week and 2 days, so you count 2 days on. Now count the extra days from Monday.
quiz.explain: 10 ÷ 7 = 1 remainder 3. After 1 week it is Monday again. Three more days: Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday.

quiz.q: It is Saturday. What day will it be in 30 days?
hints: Divide 30 by 7 and look at the remainder.
30 ÷ 7 = 4 remainder 2. Count on that many days.
Example: from Thursday, 40 days on: 40 ÷ 7 = 5 remainder 5, so count 5 days on. Count on from Saturday here.
quiz.explain: 30 ÷ 7 = 4 remainder 2. Four weeks later it is Saturday again. Two more days: Sunday, Monday.
